name: Canari
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Canari extinct, attested mainly via toponyms per Glottolog (Paz y Mino 1961, Jijon y Caamano 1919); no phonological description

sources.citation: Cabrera Moreno, Sandra Leonor. 2025. 'Morphological contextualization of Cañari family names in the Southern Andes of Ecuador.' Universidad-Verdad 87: 152ff. doi:10.33324/uv.vi87.1074.
sources.note: Anthroponymy only; the single 'stressed syllable' mention (p. 157) is about Dutch/German trochees, not Cañari.

sources.citation: Encalada Vásquez, Oswaldo. 2021. Los cañaris y su lengua. Cuenca: UCuenca Press (Universidad de Cuenca). ISBN 978-9978-14-467-1. ~280 pp. (142 PDF spreads).
sources.note: Sec. 3.0 (p. 65) states outright that the phonological system of Cañari cannot be known; the book is a toponymic-root study. Only accent remarks are per-toponym: sec. 3.6.13 (p. 148) says the root -déleg 'plain' was originally paroxytone (grave) but now also appears oxytone (Chordeleg); a note in ch. 4 says 'cañaro' is also pronounced proparoxytone. No general word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Encalada Vásquez, Oswaldo. 2021. Los vestigios de la lengua puruhá. Cuenca: Universidad del Azuay Casa Editora. doi:10.33324/ceuazuay.161. 140 pp.
sources.note: Sister language Puruhá; 54 mentions of Cañari, none about accent; grep for acento/tónica/aguda/esdrújula returns nothing relevant.

sources.citation: Encalada Vásquez, Oswaldo. 2026. Tumipanpasuyu: historia y toponimia. Cuenca: Universidad del Azuay Casa Editora. ISBN 978-9942-54-068-3. 180 pp.
sources.note: Toponymy of the Tomebamba/Cuenca region; no accent statement (grep for acento etc. returns nothing).
Consonant inventory from Howard 2010 and a note that Cañari/Puruhá had word-initial voiced stops and /ž/; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Cordero, Guillermo. 2022. 'Los cañaris y su lengua: entrevista a Oswaldo Encalada Vásquez.' Revista Pucara 32: 211-217.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; discusses roots (-zhuma, -shún 'hill') and research history.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page cana1260 (refs: Howard 2010, Floyd 2022, Paz y Miño 1961, Jijón y Caamaño 1919).
sources.note: Language extinct, existence verified mainly through toponyms; no descriptive reference of grammar/phonology type.
